Lakeshore Imaging
MRI Lumbar Spine Without Contrast
Patient: Morgan Ashby-Vale
Date of Birth: 02/17/1981
Date of Service: 04/18/2025
Ordering Provider: Dr. Ines Castellanos-Reyes

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Patient is a 44 year old male presenting with complaints of low back pain and left calf numbness.
The symptoms began following an injury sustained at his place of employment.
He reports pain radiating down the left leg.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the lumbar spine was performed without the use of intravenous contrast.
The examination included axial, sagittal, and coronal views of the L1 through S1 levels.
The patient was adequately prepared and positioned for the study.

COMPARISON:
No prior relevant imaging was available for comparison.

FINDINGS:
The overall alignment of the lumbar spine appears maintained.
There is mild degenerative change noted at the lower vertebral levels.
The L1-L2 intervertebral disc shows normal disc height and signal.
L4-L5: 4 mm posterior central disc protrusion contacting the thecal sac.
L5-S1: mild disc desiccation without protrusion.
No evidence of significant spinal canal stenosis at any level.
No fracture or listhesis.

IMPRESSION:
1. Central disc protrusion at L4-L5 causing contact with the thecal sac.
2. Mild degenerative disc disease at L5-S1.
3. No acute osseous abnormality identified.

Radiologist: Dr. Ansgar Velloso-Krantz, MD
